chapters.label: Roots
chapters.summary: I came to engineering through design, and I still think like an artist.
details: , 2013. I studied design before I wrote any production code.

The thing I learned in school and have carried through my whole career is the concept: what are you building, and why? What is it trying to say or solve? Once that is clear, I use any and all tools to get there.

chapters.label: TrueCar
chapters.summary: The go-to frontend engineer on a platform migration for 600+ partners. Two hackathon wins.
details: I worked on four product teams in four years and was promoted along the way. Every move meant a new codebase, and I was productive fast each time.

The company moved its Multi-Partner Platform off a legacy stack to React/Redux, with Node.js middleware and Cypress test coverage. I was the go-to CSS and frontend engineer, which is why they pulled me onto it. I led the frontend side: the assets, the components, and a one-to-one check of the new build against the legacy code. The platform got faster, more reliable, and quicker to release for every partner on it.
My team won the TrueCar Hackathon in 2017 and again in 2019.
I shared frontend practices through pairing and code reviews, and I mentored the junior developers coming up behind me.

chapters.label: Tradesy
chapters.summary: Sole engineer on a growth team at a resale marketplace. Owned the move to React.
details: As the growth team's only engineer, I built the influencer pages myself. I learned PHP backend work so I could ship every feature end to end.
I owned the migration of the legacy frontend to React.
I set up a shared component library along the way, so new features started from common parts instead of from scratch.

chapters.label: Wildland fire
chapters.summary: Some time on a wildland fire crew: academy, engine, then a hotshot crew. Top Cadet, then Rookie of the Year.
details: I stepped away from software to fight wildfire. I trained at the Rio Hondo Wildland Fire Academy and graduated Top Cadet in 2022.
I spent a year on Engine 324, filling in on a hotshot crew twice, then a year on the Trinity hotshot crew. Trinity named me Rookie of the Year for first-year leadership.
I worked long assignments in remote terrain where the stakes were high, on a tight crew where every role depended on the others. The lesson I brought back: stay calm, and do the job in front of you.

chapters.label: Back to software
chapters.summary: I came back from the fireline to a field that had changed. For me, AI is a dream come true: a chance to grow and work twice as fast.

chapters.label: PorchPass
chapters.summary: Owned the core dealer tools and led AI adoption across the company.
details: People were running LLM experiments on their own. I turned those into shared decisions about which tools to use, how to roll them out, and how to keep them safe.
I owned the core dealer tools end to end in React/TypeScript. I built custom UI components and hardened the API integrations so the tools held up for dealer partners.

I worked with product, design, and backend to rebuild the frontend architecture around reusable components and responsive design. Features shipped faster, and the UI became consistent across the platform.

chapters.label: Titan Intake
chapters.role: Senior Software Engineer, AI, since January 2026.
chapters.summary: I build the pipeline between a product spec and shipped code.
details: I build agent pipelines that turn a product spec into tested code, and the evaluation and memory layers that help them improve over time. I also teach the team how to work with AI.

paragraphs: Software engineer since 2014, with some time on a wildland fire crew along the way. I build products people use, developer tools, and AI systems. My background is web, and I keep learning outward from it: backend systems, hardware, networking, and how they all fit together.

Outside work I balance being active with being still. In Colorado that means hiking, running and biking. I've trained in martial arts for years, most recently aikido, and I keep a Zen meditation practice. I travel often, and I'm just as happy at home or at dinner with friends.

rules.title: Rules I work by
items: With AI, experiment and test together. Build the harness around what you need to know.
Stay adaptable. Let go of what's ready to go, and learn what comes next.
Focus alone. Understand and build with a team.
Stay calm under pressure, and do the job in front of you.
